identity.title: Modeling Dust Emission of HL Tau Disk Based on Planet-Disk Interactions

paper_type_evidence.quote: We use extensive global two-dimensional hydrodynamic disk gas+dust simulations with embedded planets, coupled with three dimensional radiative transfer calculations, to model the dust ring and gap structures in the HL Tau protoplanetary disk

question.value: Can the ring and gap structures of the HL Tau disk seen by ALMA be produced by planet-disk interactions?

evidence.quote: We address the question whether the observed features of HL Tau by ALMA can be produced by planet-disk interactions.

what.value: ALMA HL Tau Band 6 and 7 continuum images, ring/gap identification and spectral index profile

evidence.quote: The simulation results are then coupled with 3D radiative transfer calculations to be compared with the observation of Partnership et al. (2015).

what.value: Initial disk model parameters (disk mass 0.135 Msun etc.)

evidence.quote: We initialize our hydrodynamic simulation using the results from (cite: Kwon2011).

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: LA-COMPASS 2D gas+dust hydrodynamic simulations with three fixed planets, post-processed with RADMC-3D at 1 mm

evidence.quote: The model adopted to analyze HL Tau observations makes use of the LA-COMPASS code (cite: Li2005; Li2009; Fu2014) to calculate the planet-disk interaction

what.value: Synthetic observation in the Fourier domain and dust opacity calculation

evidence.quote: we “observe” our models and compare them with the ALMA observations in the Fourier domain, following the procedure described in (cite: Isella2009).

unstated_but_needed: ALMA visibility data/images used and how they were obtained (project code, calibration)
Simulated observation uv coverage, inclination and PA used for the model image
Residual map details and fit quality metric

method.value: 2D polar grid LA-COMPASS with self-gravity, three fixed planets, 0.15 mm dust in short friction time approximation

evidence.quote: The disk extends from 2.4 AU to 156 AU, and is simulated using a polar grid containing 3072 and 768 cells in the radial and azimuthal direction, respectively.

key_parameters.value: alpha = 1e-3; M_disk ~7.35e-2 Msun; M* = 0.55 Msun; planets 0.35, 0.17, 0.26 MJup at 13.1, 33.0, 68.6 AU

evidence.quote: Hence we reduce the disk mass to be $M_{\rm{disk}} \approx 7.35 \times 10^{-2}$ $M_{\odot}$

assumptions.value: Initial dust-to-gas ratio of 1%, no migration

evidence.quote: with an initial dust-to-gas ratio of $1\%$

validation.value: Planet masses chosen by tens of runs to match gap widths and depths

evidence.quote: we have performed tens of disk+planet hydro simulations in order to determine the likely planet mass values

method.value: RADMC-3D thermal Monte Carlo for dust temperature, then ray tracing at 1 mm and Fourier-domain comparison

evidence.quote: We set up a thermal Monte Carlo run to calculate the dust temperature using the radiative transfer code *RADMC-3D*.

key_parameters.value: opacity 4.6 cm2/g at 1 mm; MRN n(a)∝a^-3.5, 5e-4 to 10 mm; f_sett = 0.1

evidence.quote: The resulting dust opacity at the wavelength of 1 mm is 4.6 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$

assumptions.value: Silicates, organic carbonates and water ice grains

evidence.quote: assuming that dust grains are compact spheres made of astronomical silicates (cite: wd01),

validation.value: Compared with ALMA Band 7 image, major-axis profile, and spectral index

evidence.quote: Overall, our model reproduces the observations quite well.
makes use of the LA-COMPASS code (cite: Li2005; Li2009; Fu2014) to calculate the planet-disk interaction
radiative transfer code *RADMC-3D*[^1] to calculate the disk temperature and emission at 1 mm
three planets with masses 0.35, 0.17, and 0.26 $M_{Jup}$ at 13.1, 33.0, and 68.6 AU, respectively
We obtain the eccentricities of gaps as 0.246, 0.274 and 0.277, respectively
whereas the eccentricities of rings as 0.191, 0.079 and 0.157, respectively

findings_qualitative.value: Disk self-gravity is essential to produce the third gap; halving planet masses fails to produce the second gap; lower viscosity makes gaps too deep

evidence.quote: Run2, where the disk self-gravity is turned off, fails to produce the third gap.

claims.hypothesis: Planet-disk interactions can produce the HL Tau rings and gaps
claims.experiment: 2D gas+dust hydro with three planets plus RADMC-3D synthetic observation compared with ALMA
claims.result: Model matches major-axis intensity profile, spectral index and gap eccentricity trend at three main gaps
claims.finding: Observed features can be mostly reproduced by three planets

evidence.quote: we find that the observed features can indeed be mostly reproduced by planet-disk interactions.

limitations_admitted.value: Planets fixed in radius would migrate; outer rings not reproduced with a single outer planet; disk barely stable

evidence.quote: the three planets in our model are assumed to stay on fixed radii. When allowed to migrate, they eventually move out of the current locations.

referee_caveats_inferred: No formal goodness-of-fit or parameter uncertainties; planet masses hand-tuned and degenerate with viscosity, disk mass

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: small if only the published images are used
reproducibility.score_reason: Simulation parameters are largely given, but code, ALMA data details and fit metrics are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main result is simulation-based with hand-tuned fit and unreleased code; ALMA data not specified.

methods_papers.why: Opacity calculation and Fourier-domain comparison procedure

related_projects_or_surveys: ALMA HL Tau Long Baseline Campaign
